source.author: lucr
source.text: veridicis igitur purgavit pectora dictis et finem statuit cuppedinis atque timoris exposuitque bonum summum, quo tendimus omnes, quid foret, atque viam monstravit, tramite parvo qua possemus ad id recto contendere cursu, quidve mali foret in rebus mortalibus passim, quod fieret naturali varieque volaret seu casu seu vi, quod sic natura parasset, et quibus e portis occurri cuique deceret, et genus humanum frustra plerumque probavit volvere curarum tristis in pectore fluctus.
source.text_original: veridicis igitur purgavit pectora dictis / et finem statuit cuppedinis atque timoris / exposuitque bonum summum, quo tendimus omnes, / quid foret, atque viam monstravit, tramite parvo / qua possemus ad id recto contendere cursu, / quidve mali foret in rebus mortalibus passim, / quod fieret naturali varieque volaret / seu casu seu vi, quod sic natura parasset, / et quibus e portis occurri cuique deceret, / et genus humanum frustra plerumque probavit / volvere curarum tristis in pectore fluctus.
source.text_english: Thus he purified their hearts with truthful words, set a limit to desire and fear, and explained what the highest good was, the goal toward which we all strive; and he showed the way by which, along a small path, we might press on to it in a straight course, and what evil there was in mortal affairs everywhere, which came about by natural causes and wandered in various ways, either by chance or by force, as nature had thus prepared it, and from which gates it was fitting to meet each danger. And he showed that the human race, for the most part, vainly rolls the sad waves of cares in its breast.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: hunc sequamur omnes, hunc audiamus, huic deuotissime pareamus, quoniam solus, ut ait Lucretius, ueridicis hominum purgauit pectora dictis et finem statuit cuppedinis atque timoris exposuitque bonum summum, quo tendimus omnes, quid foret, atque uiam monstrauit, limite paruo qua possemus ad id recto contendere cursu.
reuse.text_original: hunc sequamur omnes, hunc audiamus, huic deuotissime pareamus, quoniam solus, ut ait Lucretius, ueridicis hominum purgauit pectora dictis et finem statuit cuppedinis atque timoris exposuitque bonum summum, quo tendimus omnes, quid foret, atque uiam monstrauit, limite paruo qua possemus ad id recto contendere cursu.
reuse.text_english: Let us all follow him, let us listen to him, let us obey him most devoutly, since he alone, as Lucretius says, has purified the hearts of men with truthful words and has set an end to desire and dispelled fear and has shown what the highest good would be, toward which we all strive, and has pointed out the way by which, over a short stretch, we might be able to press on to it by a straight course.
